author: high
claim: For a sequence x_1,...,x_{n^2+1} of distinct real numbers, let a_i be the maximum length of a strictly increasing subsequence ending at x_i and b_i the maximum length of a strictly decreasing subsequence ending at x_i. Then the pairs (a_i,b_i) are pairwise distinct.
evidence: Fix indices i<j. Distinctness gives exactly one of x_i<x_j and x_i>x_j. If x_i<x_j, append x_j to a longest strictly increasing subsequence ending at x_i; this yields a strictly increasing subsequence ending at x_j of length a_i+1, so a_j>=a_i+1 and a_j!=a_i. If x_i>x_j, append x_j to a longest strictly decreasing subsequence ending at x_i; then b_j>=b_i+1 and b_j!=b_i. Hence (a_i,b_i)!=(a_j,b_j) whenever i<j.

links.statement: The endpoint rank-pair map i -> (a_i,b_i) is injective.

glossary.n: the positive integer in the theorem
glossary.x_i: the real number in position i of the sequence
glossary.a_i: the maximum length of a strictly increasing subsequence ending at position i
glossary.b_i: the maximum length of a strictly decreasing subsequence ending at position i
